# NOTES: "The Yellow House; Master of Men" by E. Phillips Oppenheim (single volume, no BOOK headings)

Gutenberg #41402. Title page: THE YELLOW HOUSE / MASTER OF MEN, VOLUME ONE, P. F. Collier & Son, 1908/1912. Narrator: Kate Ffolliot (first person). Everything below is Kate's narration unless noted.

## Cast
- **Kate Ffolliot**: narrator, ~20s, pale, black-haired, lived abroad (school in Berlin, Heidelberg; took good degree at Heidelberg). Restless, proud, sharp-tongued. Later becomes secretary to Adelaide Fortress; engaged to Bruce Deville.
- **Alice Ffolliot**: youngest sister, homely, literal, conventional, pious, parish helper, "domestic," sings voluntary at organ.
- **Horace Ffolliot** ("my father"; Canon Ffolliot at Eastminster; secret name **Philip Maltabar**): tall, slim, clean-shaven, grey eyes, hair parted in middle, fastidious, great preacher, weak lung/side wound. Former parish Belchester (suburban, two curates). Wrote sermons. Formerly "Philip Maltabar," lover of Adelaide Fortress; killed Stephen Berdenstein.
- **Mary**: their maid. **Morris**: servant (gave letters through window).
- **Lady Amy Naselton** (of Naselton Hall, ~12 miles; "Amy Naselton"): middle-aged, bright, gossip, matchmaker; husband Naselton; son **Fred** Naselton (was in Rio, met Berdenstein). Godmother to Bruce Deville.
- **The Countess** of Sysington Hall (12 miles away), with two anæmic daughters.
- **Holgates of Holgate Brand**, **Lady Romney**, **Lady Applecorn** (barouche, eyeglass), **Mr. Charlsworth** (churchwarden), **Mr. Hewitt** (schools, ventilators), **Harrison** (small tenant farmer who sets traps), **Colonel Dacre** (busybody who wrote to Bishop), **Mr. Densham** (Socialist candidate, Belchester), **Mr. Harris** (Greek; Adelaide's manuscript), **Morris** (informant), **Grant's farm** (rooms for Adelaide), **Lady Bolton** (Eastminster), **Bishop of Exchester** (visited, offered canonry).
- **Bruce Deville** ("Mr. Bruce Deville," of Deville Court, "Bruce"; godson of Lady Naselton): tall, very broad, ragged beard, long hair, grey piercing eyes, untidy, shabby shooting coat, beagles (dogs: **Lawless**, **Marvel**, **Madam**), beagling after hares; horse **Diana** (chestnut). Lord of Manor of a dozen parishes; "poor" in reputation. Father: **Mr. Bromley Deville** (Adelaide's father's oldest friend; executor). Once spent fortune on singer **Marie Leparte**. Saved Olive's life at Baeren (Italian lakes/Switzerland) by stopping runaway horses; then walked to Geneva.
- **Adelaide Fortress** (Mrs., "Marcia"; Kate's mother): ~35-40, plain-but-striking, thin, brown hair with grey, dark bright eyes, gleaming teeth? (no—Olive has teeth). Socialist, former journalist, correspondent for a daily, electioneered for Mr. Densham at Belchester (~4,000 votes). Lives at **the Yellow House** (oddly shaped, yellow, near plantation, between Vicarage and Deville Court). Lived as Horace's partner unmarried; has "shame." Her father's old friend link to Bruce. Writes for newspapers; sees Kate as secretary; London flat ready; Victoria Street (mother's address in London).
- **Olive Berdenstein** (Miss Berdenstein): short, dark, thin, sallow, gleaming white teeth, black eyes, diamonds, sealskin coat, over-dressed; loves Bruce Deville; rich (~£1 million, diamonds, "Rio"). Sister of **Stephen Berdenstein**.
- **Stephen Berdenstein**: sallow, Jewish-type features, black eyes, teeth, cane, South America (Rio, "Rio Janeiro") for many years; formerly loved Adelaide; enemy of Philip Maltabar; struck at Horace with knife; killed in plantation near Yellow House on Sunday; found dead, then dragged to church porch; cried "Judas!" in church.
- **Mr. Smith**: plainclothes detective.

## Chronology / Events (Book)
1. **Ch I**: Family settled at Vicarage (small country vicarage, Northshire; church, cedar trees, lawn, steep drive). Callers come: Countess, Holgates, Lady Naselton. Two non-callers: Bruce Deville and the woman in the Yellow House. Lady Naselton gossips: woman followed Bruce, lived near his gates, furniture from Court; Bruce is godson, "brutal," slouches, ruined by Marie Leparte, spent 12 years abroad. Father faints/pales at name "Bruce Deville." Father: "Under which circumstances... avoid him."
2. **Ch II**: Kate sees Alice, sour talk. At gate, Kate sees Bruce and woman (unnamed) with beagles in lane; Bruce: "pale-faced, black-haired chit." Father faints by garden, hears "her voice" through shadows; asks where she is.
3. **Ch III**: Sunday. Lady Naselton approves father's sermon. Beagle Lawless with broken leg at Vicarage; Kate binds it. Bruce brusque; Harrison's traps; "Ffolliot? How do you spell it?" Father meets Bruce: "I desire no welcome from you." Father: Bruce "closely associated with the most unhappy chapter of my life." "Until the end..."
4. **Ch IV**: Kate caught in storm at Yellow House; Adelaide. Adelaide: Socialist; Belchester election. Study with Marcia's things; Bruce there reading manuscript for "Harris" (Greek). Bruce escapes out window. Father bursts in: "Your daughter... at once"; Adelaide: "I presume that I am addressing Mr. Ffolliot." Father: "Marcia!" "You had better go." Bruce crosses park toward her.
5. **Ch V**: South American letter to father, large square envelope, fine writing, "London about fifteenth." Father leaves for London (Annesly Junction 3.30; St. Pancras 7.50). Kate sees Bruce drop envelope same handwriting. Alice: father previously went to London often at Belchester.
6. **Ch VI**: Lady Naselton's tea (Thursday). Millionaire **Mr. Berdenstein** (Stephen) introduced: tall, dark, sallow, teeth. Reveals: arrived London ~15th, Rio, Fred Naselton, sister in Paris, "Adelaide Fortress," "I am going to regain her or die." Asks Kate not to tell Adelaide he's back; says father not telling her. Hints Bruce "certain reasons" to keep silent.
7. **Ch VII**: Saturday; father not returned. Kate goes to Yellow House; Bruce and Adelaide there. Kate accuses them, says Berdenstein at Naselton Hall (breaks promise). Adelaide: "Avoid that man Berdenstein like a pestilence... bitter enemies." Kate sees father walking up road with revolver. Father's face aged.
8. **Ch VIII**: Sunday. Lady Naselton: Bishop of Exchester visiting; cathedral stalls vacant. Kate meets Berdenstein-"Stephen" with father on Bromilow Downs; Kate tells father of Berdenstein; father sends Kate to Mr. Charlsworth, walks off with Stephen toward Deville Court. ("Welcome to England once more, Stephen.")
9. **Ch IX**: Evensong sermon, "The wages of sin is death." Stephen staggers in bleeding, cries "Judas! you, Judas! Oh! my God!" and dies. Carried to churchyard. Bishop: "struggling for sanctuary." Adelaide kneels by him.
10. **Ch X**: Kate ill a week. Bruce sends roses (Adelaide's idea), calls daily. Father to be made canon. Inquest: murder in plantation between downs and Yellow House. Money/watch found. Kate realizes father was there.
11. **Ch XI**: Father admits knowing Berdenstein; refuses to say more; Kate extracts promise of silence; threatens to leave for Dresden/Eastminster.
12. **Ch XII**: Olive Berdenstein visits Vicarage; identifies brother by watch; seeks "Philip Maltabar," enemy; father refuses to see her. She searches card-plate.
13. **Ch XIII**: Father: "vengeance belongs to God." Kate meets Bruce on road; banter; "I want to ask you just one thing about that man."
14. **Ch XIV**: Father bandaged wound (knife/blow, side), refuses doctor; says "attack the night before I returned." Kate meets Bruce; he warns her; they reach Yellow House; Olive is there. "At last!"
15. **Ch XV**: Olive tells story of Baeren/ Swiss horses; Bruce saved her. Olive finds photograph in secret cabinet of **Philip Maltabar**, Adelaide denies.
16. **Ch XVI**: Kate sees photograph: it is her father, "It was my father."
17. **Ch XVII**: Bruce walks Kate home. Father: "There is a secret... not mine to tell." Kate threatens to leave; father says "stay."
18. **Ch XVIII**: Kate's jealousy. Olive's status: rooms at Grant's farm; Bruce's "shake hands" request.
19. **Ch XIX**: Adelaide tells story: journalist; coterie; marriage refused; man (Horace) became clergyman; she left him for another. "You are my child--and his!"
20. **Ch XX**: Kate: "I am the victim." Olive arrives with Bruce (Bruce seems to take Olive home). Kate notes Adelaide watching.
21. **Ch XXI**: Father gone to London (telegram); letter from "London," then will go to sea. Kate learns Bromley Deville executor. Walk with Bruce, violets, "Diana." Olive confronts Kate and Bruce on Vicarage road; threatens magistrate.
22. **Ch XXII**: Olive's "compact" offer: Kate keeps away from Bruce; Olive will leave Maltabar alone. Kate promises. Olive: "I shall die if he does not care."
23. **Ch XXIII**: Week of avoidance; Bruce calls. Adelaide offers secretary job (£60/yr, typewriting). Bruce confronts Kate in plantation; Kate reaches Vicarage gate; Olive approaches; Bruce greets her.
24. **Ch XXIV**: Kate accepts Adelaide's secretary job. Olive visits Kate: confesses she loves Bruce, threatens to kill Kate, offers £10,000 if Bruce proposes and Kate refuses.
25. **Ch XXV**: Bruce proposes to Kate. Kate lies: "I do not care for you." He leaves.
26. **Ch XXVI**: Kate visits Adelaide; announces she'll move to London. Adelaide: Bruce "consoling himself"; Adelaide says Bruce heard Berdenstein threaten; "We will go away."
27. **Ch XXVII** (London): Kate sees father in Commercial Road, Whitechapel, dressed poor. Telegrams: Bruce ("Can answer for it she has taken no steps"), Olive ("I have no intention of breaking our compact"). Father's letter from Ventnor, dated three days earlier, promises return Monday.
28. **Ch XXVIII** (Eastminster): Alice's letter: father back, preached. Kate walks; meets Bruce; he says Olive has gone to London/ Paris; he proposes again; Kate accepts ("my lover"), they kiss. Olive appears at close: "a little call," will call again.
29. **Ch XXIX**: Evensong; Olive in cathedral recognizes Horace; sermon of farewell. Olive at study: "Have you forgotten me, Philip Maltabar?" Father confesses killing Stephen ("blow for blow," Stephen's knife at his heart, Stephen earlier attempted murder in London). Olive leaves threatening police.
30. **Ch XXX**: Father's letter: leaves Eastminster forever; memoir to Bishop; "side of my life... not disgraceful." Kate follows; Alice stays. Olive walks with Kate to station, says Bruce is at station with tickets. Kate and Bruce to London; Colville Hall (East End). Father preaches farewell to working-class audience; collapses in side room; "God is very good... There was nothing I wished for but to see you once more." Olive: "I forgive. Farewell." Police come; Olive says "This is not the man." Father dies: "This is happiness."

## Key quoted phrases
- "Judas! you, Judas! Oh! my God!" (Stephen)
- "The wages of sin is death." (father's text)
- "London about the 15th" (envelope)
- "Marcia!" (father to Adelaide)
- "It was my father." (Kate, ch XVI)
- "This is happiness." (father, last words)

## Places
Vicarage (Northshire, near Deville Court and Yellow House); Naselton Hall (red chimneys on hillside); Deville Court; Yellow House (plantation footpath between); Bromilow Downs; Annesly Junction; St. Pancras; Belchester; Eastminster (cathedral, Bishop of Exchester); Ventnor; Commercial Road, Whitechapel; Colville Hall; Victoria Street (London); Baeren (Italian lakes); Geneva; Mellborough; Grant's farm; Bromilow.
